ESR1.role: Estrogen-dependent follicular maturation, ovulation, and endometrial receptivity
ESR1.logic: Estrogen receptor alpha mediates estradiol signaling that drives follicular maturation, ovulation, and endometrial receptivity. Antagonism or modulation of ERalpha disrupts estradiol-dependent folliculogenesis and the ovulatory cycle.

ESR1.logic_cited: Estrogen receptor alpha mediates estradiol signaling[2] that drives follicular maturation, ovulation, and endometrial receptivity. Antagonism or modulation of ERalpha disrupts estradiol-dependent folliculogenesis and the ovulatory cycle[3t][44!].

DRD2.role: Dopaminergic regulation of prolactin secretion from anterior pituitary lactotrophs
DRD2.logic: The D2 dopamine receptor mediates tonic dopaminergic inhibition of prolactin release from anterior pituitary lactotrophs. D2 antagonism removes this inhibition, causing hyperprolactinemia that suppresses GnRH pulsatility and gonadotropin secretion.
DRD2.role_cited: Dopaminergic regulation of prolactin secretion from anterior pituitary lactotrophs[4t]
DRD2.logic_cited: The D2 dopamine receptor mediates tonic dopaminergic inhibition[4t] of prolactin release from anterior pituitary lactotrophs[4]. D2 antagonism removes this inhibition[5t], causing hyperprolactinemia that suppresses GnRH pulsatility and gonadotropin secretion[6].

CYP17A1.role: Gonadal and adrenal steroidogenesis converting pregnenolone to DHEA and androstenedione
CYP17A1.logic: CYP17A1 (17alpha-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase) catalyzes a committed step of gonadal and adrenal steroidogenesis, converting pregnenolone toward DHEA and androstenedione. Its inhibition blocks androgen biosynthesis upstream of both testosterone and estradiol, depleting sex steroids.

CYP17A1.logic_cited: CYP17A1 (17alpha-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase) catalyzes a committed step of gonadal and adrenal steroidogenesis[7], converting pregnenolone toward DHEA and androstenedione[7t]. Its inhibition blocks androgen biosynthesis upstream of both testosterone and estradiol[8], depleting sex steroids[9t].

CYP19A1.role: Conversion of androgens to estrogens in ovarian granulosa cells and testicular tissue
CYP19A1.logic: Aromatase (CYP19A1) converts androgens to estrogens in ovarian granulosa cells and testicular tissue. Its inhibition lowers estradiol, impairing follicular development and ovulation and disrupting the menstrual and estrous cycle.
CYP19A1.role_cited: Conversion of androgens to estrogens in ovarian granulosa cells and testicular tissue[10t][11t]
CYP19A1.logic_cited: Aromatase (CYP19A1) converts androgens to estrogens in ovarian granulosa cells and testicular tissue[10][11]. Its inhibition lowers estradiol[12], impairing follicular development and ovulation[45!] and disrupting the menstrual and estrous cycle.

SRD5A2.role: Conversion of testosterone to DHT in prostate and reproductive tissues
SRD5A2.logic: 5alpha-reductase type 2 (SRD5A2) converts testosterone to the more potent androgen DHT in reproductive tissues. Its inhibition lowers DHT, reducing androgen-dependent maturation and secretory function of male reproductive tissues.
SRD5A2.role_cited: Conversion of testosterone to DHT in prostate[13t] and reproductive tissues[13t]
SRD5A2.logic_cited: 5alpha-reductase type 2 (SRD5A2) converts testosterone to the more potent androgen DHT[14c] in reproductive tissues[13][14c]. Its inhibition lowers DHT[14c], reducing androgen-dependent maturation and secretory function of male reproductive tissues[14c].

OPRM1.logic: The mu-opioid receptor modulates the hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator. Its activation inhibits GnRH release, lowering pituitary LH and FSH output and producing a hypogonadotropic, hypogonadal state in both sexes.
OPRM1.logic_cited: The mu-opioid receptor modulates the hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator[17t]. Its activation inhibits GnRH release[17], lowering pituitary LH and FSH output[15!] and producing a hypogonadotropic, hypogonadal state in both sexes[18t][19t].

pathway_rules: Direct germ-cell cytotoxicity: DNA-reactive alkylating agents and antimetabolites deplete spermatogonial stem cells and primordial follicles. This mechanism is read from the reactive chemistry of the molecule itself and operates without any receptor, so weak or failed binding to the receptors listed above does not argue against it.

Sex-steroid signaling: engagement of the androgen, estrogen or progesterone receptor, or inhibition of the steroidogenic enzymes CYP17A1, CYP19A1, CYP11B1 or SRD5A2, alters circulating testosterone and estradiol and their gonadotropin feedback, impairing spermatogenesis, folliculogenesis and ovulation.

Hypothalamic-pituitary suppression: centrally acting mu-opioid agonists lower GnRH pulse frequency, and D2 receptor blockade raises prolactin, which inhibits GnRH neurons. Both produce hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with amenorrhoea or reduced testosterone.

Prostaglandin-dependent reproduction: COX inhibition prevents the periovulatory prostaglandin rise required for follicular rupture, giving luteinized unruptured follicles and reversible anovulation, while prostanoid analogs acting at uterotonic or luteolytic receptors cause myometrial contraction, luteolysis and pregnancy loss.

Sympathetic control of emission: alpha1-adrenoceptor blockade prevents contraction of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and bladder neck, producing anejaculation or retrograde ejaculation with reduced semen volume.

Sertoli-cell and germ-cell support: depletion of glycosphingolipids or disruption of the blood-testis barrier and Sertoli-cell junctions blocks spermatid maturation and causes oligospermia even when circulating hormones are unchanged.

Exposure at the gonad is required: agents with negligible systemic absorption, peripherally restricted distribution, or a single subpharmacologic diagnostic dose do not reach hypothalamic, pituitary or gonadal tissue at concentrations able to perturb gametogenesis.

Target-tissue expression governs reproductive risk: when a drug's established molecular target (bacterial cell-wall enzymes, platelet purinergic or coagulation proteins, renal tubular transporters, viral polymerases, incretin enzymes, trigeminovascular receptors) is absent from the hypothalamus, pituitary, gonad and germinal epithelium, the HPG axis and gametogenesis remain intact. Docking places every ligand into every pocket, so a favorable score for such a drug is a geometric artifact rather than evidence of a reproductive mechanism.

yes_features: Aziridine, thiophosphoramide, chloroethyl mustard or oxazaphosphorine, methanesulfonate, nitrosourea or triazene alkylating groups: crosslink and alkylate DNA in spermatogonia and oocytes, causing dose-dependent and often irreversible germ-cell loss.

Antifolate pteridines, halogenated pyrimidines, thiopurines and other nucleobase analogs, hydroxamic acid or hydroxyurea ribonucleotide-reductase inhibitors, and nucleoside analogs accepted as substrates by host DNA polymerases: arrest DNA synthesis in dividing germ cells, producing oligospermia and follicle depletion.

Intact C18 estrane, C19 androstane or 19-nor progestin steroid nuclei bearing a 3-keto-delta4 or 3-hydroxy aromatic A ring: bind the androgen, estrogen or progesterone receptor and exert gonadotropin negative feedback that suppresses endogenous spermatogenesis and ovulation.
Triazolyl- or imidazolyl-methyl groups on a compact benzonitrile or benzyl scaffold, and 6-methylene or 6-alkyl androstenedione analogs: inhibit CYP19A1 aromatase and deplete estradiol.

Imidazole ring with a free basic N3 embedded in a lipophilic dichlorophenyl-dioxolane or aryl-ketone framework: coordinates the heme iron of human CYP17A1 and CYP11B1 and blocks gonadal and adrenal steroid synthesis.

Phenothiazine, thioxanthene, dibenzoxazepine, butyrophenone or substituted-benzamide cores carrying a basic amine two to three carbons from the ring system: high-affinity D2 antagonism causing hyperprolactinemia and secondary hypogonadism.

Morphinan, orvinol, 4-anilidopiperidine or 4-phenylpiperidine opioid agonist pharmacophores that are lipophilic enough to enter the CNS: activate hypothalamic mu-opioid receptors and lower GnRH pulse frequency.

Arylpropionic acid, arylacetic acid or indole-3-acetic acid cyclooxygenase pharmacophores: suppress the periovulatory prostaglandin surge needed for follicular rupture, causing reversible anovulation.

Prostanoid scaffolds with a cyclopentane core and a 15-hydroxy omega chain acting at uterotonic or luteolytic receptors, such as PGF2alpha analogs bearing an isopropyl ester and EP3-active PGE analogs: induce myometrial contraction, luteolysis and pregnancy loss.

4-Amino-6,7-dimethoxyquinazoline alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonists, and 4-azasteroid or benzoquinolinone 5alpha-reductase inhibitors: impair seminal emission and androgen-dependent maturation of the male accessory glands.
no_features: Fused beta-lactam bicyclic cores (penam penicillins, cephem cephalosporins): inhibit bacterial transpeptidases that have no mammalian counterpart, and animal reproduction studies show no impairment of fertility.

Thienopyridine or ATP-analog P2Y12 ligands, 4-hydroxycoumarin vitamin-K-epoxide-reductase inhibitors, and PAR-1 antagonists: platelet and coagulation targets are not expressed in the hypothalamus, pituitary, gonad or germinal epithelium.

Triazole azoles bearing three ring nitrogens on an extended lipophilic antifungal scaffold, and allylamine squalene-epoxidase inhibitors: selective for fungal CYP51 or fungal squalene epoxidase and spare human CYP17A1 and CYP19A1 at therapeutic exposure.

Nucleoside and nucleotide analogs that require viral kinase activation or act selectively on viral polymerase or reverse transcriptase, and non-nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitors: poor substrates for host DNA polymerases, so germ-cell genomic DNA is not modified.
Unsubstituted sulfamoyl carbonic-anhydrase inhibitors and sulfamoyl or aryloxyacetic loop-diuretic scaffolds: act on renal tubular enzymes and transporters and carry no endocrine or gonadal activity.
Gliptin-type DPP-4 inhibitors and related incretin-pathway antidiabetic scaffolds: confined to enteroendocrine and metabolic targets with no role in gametogenesis.
Indole or piperidine 5-HT1B/1D triptans, 5-HT1F agonists and CGRP-receptor antagonists: act on trigeminovascular and cranial vascular targets absent from the reproductive axis.
Endogenous amino acids, vitamins and cofactors, physiologic buffers and trace-element salts given at physiologic doses: substrates of normal metabolism that support rather than impair gametogenesis.

Permanently charged, strongly polar, macromolecular or otherwise peripherally restricted agents, including locally acting gastrointestinal drugs and peripherally restricted opioid receptor antagonists: do not reach hypothalamic, pituitary or gonadal compartments in pharmacologically active amounts.
Radiolabeled diagnostic imaging tracers given as a single subpharmacologic microdose: total body exposure is orders of magnitude below any threshold for a gonadal effect.

contradiction_flags.segment_text: lowering pituitary LH and FSH output

contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: Rapid frequency (more than 1 pulse per h) GnRH pulses favor LH while slower frequencies favor FSH secretion. contradiction_flags.mla: Zarn, Jürg A., et al. "Azole Fungicides Affect Mammalian Steroidogenesis by Inhibiting Sterol 14 Alpha-Demethylase and Aromatase." Environmental Health Perspectives, vol. 111, no. 3, 2003, pp. 255-61. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.5785.

contradiction_flags.segment_text: Gliptin-type DPP-4 inhibitors and related incretin-pathway antidiabetic scaffolds: confined to enteroendocrine and metabolic targets
contradiction_flags.mla: Baggio, Laurie L., and Daniel J. Drucker. "Biology of Incretins: GLP-1 and GIP." Gastroenterology, vol. 132, no. 6, 2007, pp. 2131-57. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2007.03.054.

contradiction_flags.note: The recorded quote merely identifies DPP-4 as the degrading enzyme and the rationale for gliptins, contradicting nothing. The osteoblast/adipose sentence is the one that strains the clause's exclusivity wording, though the extra target is bone rather than the reproductive axis the atom is really shielding. contradiction_flags.segment_text: confined to enteroendocrine and metabolic targets
contradiction_flags.mla: Baggio, Laurie L., and Daniel J. Drucker. "Biology of Incretins: GLP-1 and GIP." Gastroenterology, vol. 132, no. 6, 2007, pp. 2131-57. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2007.03.054.

contradiction_flags.segment_text: Endogenous amino acids, vitamins and cofactors, physiologic buffers and trace-element salts given at physiologic doses: substrates of normal metabolism that support rather than impair gametogenesis.
contradiction_flags.mla: Schisterman, Enrique F., et al. "Effect of Folic Acid and Zinc Supplementation in Men on Semen Quality and Live Birth Among Couples Undergoing Infertility Treatment: a Randomized Clinical Trial." JAMA, vol. 323, no. 1, 2020, pp. 35-48. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2019.18714.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: A statistically significant increase in DNA fragmentation was observed with folic acid and zinc supplementation (mean of 29.7% for percentage of DNA fragmentation in the folic acid and zinc group and 27.2% in the placebo group; mean difference, 2.4% [95% CI, 0.5% to 4.4%]).
contradiction_flags.note: Numbers checked in both: the trial dose is a pharmacologic supplement, not the clause's physiologic dose, so the impairment finding lies outside the clause's own dose condition. Within that dose the refutation of 'rather than impair' is real but small (2.4 percentage points). (Vitamins, cofactors and trace-element salts given at PHYSIOLOGIC doses are normal metabolic substrates that support rather than impair gametogenesis.; Folic acid 5 mg + zinc 30 mg daily significantly raised sperm DNA fragmentation (29.7% vs 27.2% placebo; difference 2.4%, 95% CI 0.5-4.4) and improved no other semen parameter and no live-birth rate.)
contradiction_flags.scope: Supplemental, above-physiologic doses (5 mg/day folic acid, about 12x the RDA; 30 mg/day elemental zinc, about 3x the RDA) for 6 months in men undergoing infertility treatment; the only impaired endpoint was sperm DNA fragmentation (+2.4 percentage points).

contradiction_flags.mla: Schisterman, Enrique F., et al. "Effect of Folic Acid and Zinc Supplementation in Men on Semen Quality and Live Birth Among Couples Undergoing Infertility Treatment: a Randomized Clinical Trial." JAMA, vol. 323, no. 1, 2020, pp. 35-48. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2019.18714.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: A statistically significant increase in DNA fragmentation was observed with folic acid and zinc supplementation (mean of 29.7% for percentage of DNA fragmentation in the folic acid and zinc group and 27.2% in the placebo group; mean difference, 2.4% [95% CI, 0.5% to 4.4%]).
contradiction_flags.note: The recorded quote is a null finding: failing to improve fertility is not incompatible with 'supports rather than impairs', since the clause never claims supplementation helps. Only the DNA-fragmentation sentence shows impairment and so refutes the clause.
